thread:
maya.s: Hi team — starting surrogacy placement in Sept and sorting leave timing. Two quick questions: 1) Does Redwood treat surrogacy placement the same as parental leave for pay/top-up and childcare stipend? 2) Can I move remaining FSA (dependent care) funds to cover a surrogate travel expense? 3) Thinking of a 50% FTE phased return for 10 weeks — any paperwork I should file now?
people-ops: Congrats, Maya! :tada: Short answers: 1) Yes, surrogacy placements are eligible for parental leave and company top-up once we receive the formal placement paperwork (agency letter/court docs). 2) Dependent care FSA is limited to qualifying dependent care; travel for a surrogate typically isn't eligible. We can route the specific expense to Benefits for a determination if you want to submit docs. 3) For a 50% FTE phased return, select "part-time return" on the internal leave request form and note the desired dates; manager sign-off is required.
payroll-bot: Important: to process top-up, upload placement docs to https://benefits.redwood.com/leave-forms and tag "Placement" before the payroll cutoff (last day of pay period that includes your first paid leave day). If docs arrive late, top-up will be delayed one pay cycle.
benefits-bot: FSA note: Dependent care FSA must be for eligible care under IRS rules. Surrogate medical/travel expenses are usually HSA/medical-eligible if tied to medical care, but not typically covered by dependent care FSA. If you want, email benefits@redwood.com with the expense details and we can evaluate.
legal: If your agency provides a placement letter, that usually suffices for payroll. If there are cross-jurisdictional elements (surrogate out-of-state or international), please loop Legal early so we can advise on documentation and any privacy clauses.
eraic-mgr: Eric here — happy to approve the part-time schedule. Maya, let's sync tomorrow to map coverage for interviews and on-call. Also, we'll document expectations for the 50% window.
maya.s: Thanks  will upload the agency letter once it arrives. If benefits says travel can't go on FSA, is there any other reimbursement support?
people-ops: We have a "family travel" discretionary fund for some surrogacy adoptions/placements in exceptional cases. It's not automatic; request via benefits@redwood.com with receipts and a brief note. Policy review may take up to 5 business days.
benefits-bot: Also check medical plan: certain travel-related medical expenses (if the surrogate requires travel for care) may be reimbursable under the medical plan or via out-of-network allowances. Send specifics and well check with the carrier.
maya.s: Great, will do. One more: while on 50% FTE, do I keep stock vesting and retirement contributions?
people-ops: Stock vesting continues unless you request a formal pause; retirement 401(k) employer contributions follow payroll amounts and will be prorated with reduced salary. We'll include exact prorated numbers in your approval email.
eric-mgr: I'll take ownership of the hiring queue and interviews. Maya, please drop a 1-pager with priorities; well reroute candidate comms to me.
maya.s: Thank you all  appreciate the clarity. Uploading docs and booking the sync now :heart:
